title: Databases, Storage & Retrieval
summary: Design, query and operate data stores from relational modeling through storage engines, replication, caching, search and object storage.

modules.title: Relational modeling & constraints
modules.summary: Represent business truth with explicit keys, constraints and relationships.
modules.why: A good schema prevents invalid states and reduces downstream code complexity.

units.title: Entities, keys & integrity constraints
units.summary: Choose identifiers and constraints that encode invariants in the database.
units.challenge: Model organisations, memberships, projects and tasks with database-enforced invariants.
units.evidence: DDL plus tests showing invalid states are rejected.

units.title: Relationships & normalization
units.summary: Separate facts cleanly while understanding the cost of joins.
units.challenge: Normalize a deliberately duplicated schema, then reintroduce one justified denormalization.

units.title: Temporal, audit & soft-delete modeling
units.summary: Model history and lifecycle without destroying query correctness.
concepts: valid time vs transaction time concept
units.challenge: Design task-history and membership-audit requirements with immutable history.

modules.title: SQL query fluency
modules.summary: Express operational and analytical questions clearly and understand their relational meaning.
modules.why: ORMs do not replace the need to read and write SQL fluently.

units.title: Joins, grouping & aggregation
units.summary: Combine related data and summarize it correctly.
units.challenge: Write a product analytics query set without ORM-generated SQL.

units.title: Subqueries, CTEs & window functions
units.summary: Use advanced SQL without hiding expensive execution patterns.
units.challenge: Implement activity ranking, running totals and hierarchical traversal queries.

units.title: Safe writes, upserts & set-based updates
units.summary: Perform writes atomically and efficiently without read-modify-write races.
units.challenge: Replace a race-prone existence-check/create flow with an atomic database operation.

modules.title: Indexes & query planning
modules.summary: Understand access paths, planner choices and why an index may or may not help.
modules.why: Performance work begins with query shape, cardinality and access path—not adding indexes blindly.

units.title: B-tree, composite & covering indexes
units.summary: Design indexes around predicates, ordering and selectivity.
units.challenge: Design indexes for five real query patterns and measure before/after.
units.evidence: EXPLAIN ANALYZE plans and write-overhead discussion.

units.title: Query planner, statistics & cardinality
units.summary: Understand why estimates drive join/order/access choices.
units.challenge: Create skewed data that causes a bad plan and fix the planner inputs/query/index.

units.title: Join algorithms & execution strategies
units.summary: Understand nested-loop, hash and merge joins at systems level.
units.challenge: Predict and observe join strategy changes under different data sizes/indexes.
units.evidence: Execution-plan analysis tied to algorithmic cost.

modules.title: Transactions, MVCC & isolation
modules.summary: Reason about concurrent transactions and the anomalies each isolation level permits.
modules.why: Database correctness is a concurrency problem, not just an ACID acronym.

units.title: ACID & transaction boundaries
units.summary: Understand atomicity/durability and define business-sized transactions.
units.challenge: Identify transaction boundaries for a membership change with audit logging.
units.evidence: Sequence diagram showing committed and rolled-back effects.

units.title: MVCC, snapshots & visibility
units.summary: Understand how readers/writers coexist without treating locks as the only mechanism.
units.challenge: Observe row versions/snapshot behaviour through concurrent sessions.
units.evidence: Timeline explaining which transaction sees which version.

units.title: Isolation levels & anomalies
units.summary: Choose isolation from invariants, not habit.
units.challenge: Reproduce non-repeatable read, write skew or lost update and fix each with appropriate technique.
units.evidence: Anomaly catalogue with minimum sufficient isolation/locking strategy.

modules.title: Database locking & concurrency control
modules.summary: Understand locks, deadlocks and optimistic/pessimistic coordination.
modules.why: Contention can turn correct database usage into severe latency or availability failure.

units.title: Locks, lock queues & deadlocks
units.summary: Understand resource locking and deadlock detection/resolution.
units.challenge: Reproduce a deadlock with two transactions and eliminate it by ordering/access changes.
units.evidence: Deadlock graph and corrected transaction order.

units.title: Optimistic vs pessimistic concurrency
units.summary: Choose between conflict detection and early exclusion.
units.challenge: Compare optimistic and pessimistic approaches for editing a hot shared record.

units.title: Connection pools as concurrency limits
units.summary: Treat DB connections as scarce resources with queueing behaviour.
units.challenge: Cause pool exhaustion with slow transactions and derive a safer pool/concurrency policy.

modules.title: Storage engines, WAL & durability
modules.summary: Understand how databases turn logical rows into pages, logs and durable state.
modules.why: Indexes, compaction, checkpoints and recovery trade-offs become clearer once the storage engine is not a black box.

units.title: Pages, buffer pools & caching
units.summary: Understand the database memory/storage boundary.
units.challenge: Explain why a query becomes slower after a cold restart despite unchanged SQL.

units.title: WAL, checkpoints & crash recovery
units.summary: Understand write-ahead logging and durable recovery.
units.challenge: Simulate abrupt database restart during writes and inspect recovery behaviour.

units.title: B-tree vs LSM-tree storage engines
units.summary: Compare read/write amplification and compaction trade-offs.
units.challenge: Choose B-tree or LSM-style storage for three workloads with different read/write patterns.

modules.title: Database replication, failover & recovery
modules.summary: Operate data across multiple copies while understanding lag and consistency.
modules.why: Replication improves availability/read scale but creates new failure and stale-read modes.

units.title: Primary/replica replication
units.summary: Understand log shipping, asynchronous lag and read replicas.
units.challenge: Design read routing that avoids stale confirmation immediately after a write.

units.title: Failover, promotion & split-brain risk
units.summary: Promote replicas safely when the old primary may still exist.
units.challenge: Walk through primary loss with ambiguous network partition and propose safe promotion steps.

units.title: Backups, restore & point-in-time recovery
units.summary: Treat restore capability—not backup creation—as the reliability goal.
units.challenge: Define and test recovery from accidental deletion at multiple recovery points.
units.evidence: Restore drill report with measured recovery time.

modules.title: Schema evolution & zero-downtime migrations
modules.summary: Change data structures while old/new application versions coexist.
modules.why: Production schemas are shared contracts that cannot be changed as if deployment were instantaneous.

units.title: Expand-and-contract migrations
units.summary: Sequence additive and destructive changes safely across rolling deploys.
units.challenge: Rename a heavily used column without downtime across two app versions.

units.title: Large backfills & online data changes
units.summary: Change billions of rows without exhausting locks, I/O or replicas.
units.challenge: Design a resumable backfill with rate control and correctness checks.
units.evidence: Backfill state model and capacity/rollback plan.

units.title: Migration verification & reconciliation
units.summary: Prove old/new representations remain equivalent during transition.
units.challenge: Plan a data migration with independent verification before cutover.
units.evidence: Verification dashboard specification and cutover checklist.

modules.title: JPA/Hibernate & persistence boundaries
modules.summary: Use ORM productivity without hiding transaction/query costs or coupling domain design to persistence mechanics.
modules.why: ORM defaults can create N+1, unexpected flushes and oversized transactions that only appear under load.

units.title: Entity mapping & persistence context
units.summary: Understand managed/detached entity lifecycle and mapping semantics.
units.challenge: Trace entity lifecycle across create/update/detach scenarios.

units.title: Fetch plans, N+1 & query shape
units.summary: Control generated SQL and avoid accidental query storms.
units.challenge: Reproduce N+1 and compare three fixes under realistic data size.

units.title: ORM transactions, locking & bulk operations
units.summary: Understand where ORM abstractions diverge from database semantics.
units.challenge: Fix a correctness/performance issue caused by hidden flush or stale persistence context.
units.evidence: Root-cause note tied to generated SQL and DB behaviour.

modules.title: NoSQL data models & trade-offs
modules.summary: Choose non-relational storage based on access patterns, scale and consistency requirements.
modules.why: NoSQL is a family of data models, not one alternative to SQL.

units.title: Key-value & document databases
units.summary: Model aggregate-shaped data around known key/document access paths.
units.challenge: Model user/session/preferences and project documents in two store styles.

units.title: Wide-column & Dynamo-style systems
units.summary: Understand partition-oriented design, quorum and denormalized query tables.
units.challenge: Design a high-write activity timeline for predictable query patterns.
units.evidence: Partition model including hotspot and repair implications.

units.title: Graph & time-series databases
units.summary: Recognize workloads where traversal or time-window operations dominate.
units.challenge: Choose between relational, graph and time-series models for authorization relationships and metrics.

modules.title: Caching architecture & correctness
modules.summary: Treat cache state as duplicated data with explicit staleness and failure rules.
modules.why: Caching can reduce latency/load while creating correctness bugs that are difficult to reproduce.

units.title: Cache-aside, read/write-through & local/distributed caches
units.summary: Choose placement and update pattern based on ownership and consistency.
units.challenge: Implement cache-aside for a read-heavy endpoint and compare with local cache.

units.title: Invalidation, staleness & consistency
units.summary: Define how stale cache entries can become and when they are unacceptable.
units.challenge: Reproduce stale overwrite/read bugs during concurrent update and cache refill.
units.evidence: Race timeline and corrected invalidation protocol.

units.title: Stampede, hot keys & cache failure
units.summary: Protect origin systems when cache popularity or availability changes abruptly.
units.challenge: Expire a hot key under load and prevent origin collapse.

modules.title: Object storage & large-file workflows
modules.summary: Store and deliver files without turning application servers into byte pipes.
modules.why: Large objects have different durability, transfer, lifecycle and security characteristics from database rows.

units.title: Object keys, metadata & pre-signed access
units.summary: Separate file bytes from application metadata and authorize direct transfer safely.
units.challenge: Implement direct browser upload/download using temporary signed access.
units.evidence: Sequence diagram showing trust boundaries and metadata ownership.

units.title: Multipart/resumable upload & range delivery
units.summary: Handle large transfers, retries and partial download efficiently.
units.challenge: Design a 20GB upload that resumes after client/network interruption.
units.evidence: Upload state machine and recovery tests.

units.title: File processing, lifecycle & CDN delivery
units.summary: Build asynchronous scanning/transcoding and cache delivery around immutable objects.
units.challenge: Design document upload through scan/preview/CDN with quarantine and deletion policy.
units.evidence: End-to-end file state machine and failure handling.

modules.title: Search systems & information retrieval
modules.summary: Understand indexing, ranking and freshness for full-text product search.
modules.why: Search is a separate retrieval system with its own consistency and relevance model.

units.title: Inverted indexes & text analysis
units.summary: Understand how documents become searchable terms/postings.
units.challenge: Build a tiny inverted index or inspect analyzer/token output for realistic text.
units.evidence: Index representation and analyzer trade-off examples.

units.title: Ranking, relevance & fuzzy matching
units.summary: Treat ranking as an evaluable product behaviour.
units.challenge: Create a relevance test set and tune ranking for project/task search.
units.evidence: Judgment set and before/after ranking metrics.

units.title: Index pipelines, pagination & consistency
units.summary: Keep search indexes synchronized while accepting controlled lag.
units.challenge: Design database-to-search indexing with replay/rebuild and no synchronous dual-write dependency.
